checks.what: french-first-republic gains country Luxembourg (12 cells, about 3,000 km2; the Grand Duchy is 2,586 km2) from habsburg-netherlands, Oct 1795. The page: 'On 1 October 1795, most of Luxembourg became part of the Département des Forêts, created on 24 October 1795'; 'Most of Luxembourg (including all of the modern Grand Duchy)'; capitulation 7 June. The duchy's Belgian part is in the ledger's Belgium gain. Published: 11 cells nobody's at the end of 1795. Stage: all 12 French 1795-1799 (Directory, then Consulate). The event acts in 1795 only.

french-first-republic gains Belgian Limburg plus a 12 km circle round Horn from the prince-bishopric of Liège, Oct 1795 (13 cells). The page: 'Its territory included most of the present Belgian provinces of Liège and Limburg'; 'In 1366, the county of Loon was annexed to the bishopric'; 'Acquired County of Horne: 1568'; 'annexed by France in 1795'. The Liège page gives the year only. Month 10 comes from the 1 October 1795 annexation of the Southern Netherlands on the Siege of Luxembourg page, and it makes no difference to the end-of-year map. Published: the 10 Limburg cells were nobody's at the end of 1795 (Liège under French occupation on 1 Jan). Stage: French. The 3 Horne-circle cells (Roermond area) were French already, so nothing is taken from Dutch or Prussian land.

south-prussia gains from kingdom-of-prussia, Sep 1793, its own 1793 found region (identical spec; 210 cells, about 53,000 km2). Prussia's Jan 1793 ledger gain had already taken this land, so the found event moved only 16 cells. The page: South Prussia 'was a province of the Kingdom of Prussia from 1793 to 1807', 'created out of territory annexed in the Second Partition'; infobox '2nd Polish Partition: 25 September 1793'; in 1793 it included 'the Poznań, Kalisz and Gniezno Voivodeships of Greater Poland', 'the lands of Sieradz and Łęczyca', 'the Kuyavian voivodeship of Brześć and Dobrzyń Land' and 'adjacent parts of the Masovian voivodeships of Płock and Rawa'; capital Poznań 1793-1795. Trial: South Prussia holds its land from 1793 (Poznań cell: Prussia 1793-94 -> South Prussia), and the 181-cell 1795 snap goes away. The 1800 end anchor is unchanged for both states.

new-east-prussia gains from kingdom-of-prussia, Oct 1795, the dossier's own ledger/1 region (a 45 km circle round Płock and a 30 km circle round Dobrzyń; 38 cells). The page: after the Third Partition 'the lands of Dobrzyń and Płock northeast of the Vistula river were transferred to New East Prussia'. The end-1799 map is identical to the published draft for both colonies. Caveat: 6 of the 7 cells (centres 19.42-20.05E, 52.27-52.51N: Gostynin, Gąbin, Sochaczew) lie SOUTH-WEST of the Vistula, beyond what the page gives New East Prussia. The over-wide circle is inherited from new-east-prussia ledger/1 and keyframe 1795, which give NEP the South Prussian land SW of the Vistula too. Clipping this entry alone would leave those 6 cells plain Prussian land beside NEP land, so no fix here. A dossier request is under problems.
